assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Grossman-Helpman work provided the canonical formal framework for how organised interests shape trade policy (protection for sale), and it also developed endogenous-growth models of trade and innovation. It has shaped both theory and empirical political economy of trade. It is a foundational, widely taught framework, and trade has had no prize since 2008.
assessment.attribution: The core contributions are joint and sustained over decades, so two laureates is a clean and defensible attribution. Helpman's separate heterogeneous-firm work (B020) is a different strand and is not needed for this case.
assessment.maturity: The contributions date mainly from the 1990s and have long been tested, extended and applied. There is no timing concern.
uncertainties: Empirical support for the protection-for-sale prediction is mixed in some applications.
Overlap with the firm-heterogeneity strand could shift the committee's preferred framing toward B020.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based account of technology and labour demand, together with the China-shock evidence on local labour-market adjustment, has changed how economists and policymakers think about inequality, automation and trade. It has large empirical and policy influence and combines credible identification with a clear conceptual framework.
assessment.attribution: Autor is central to both the task-based and trade-shock strands. Hanson and Dorn are essential to the China-shock research design. Katz is a major figure for earlier skill-biased change work, but the three-name limit and his presence in B014 argue for omitting him. Acemoglu's related task framework is outside this credited list.
assessment.maturity: The research has accumulated roughly two decades of follow-up, replication and critique. It is mature enough for recognition, though some findings are still debated.
uncertainties: The three-name cap forces a choice among strong contributors, and the task-model credit overlaps with work by others outside the list.
Reassessments of the long-run persistence of China-shock effects remain ongoing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work built modern political economics, applying formal and empirical methods to how electoral rules, constitutions, fiscal institutions and state capacity shape policy outcomes. It is broad, unified in method and influential across economics and political science.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the central figures for the constitutions and electoral-rules programme. Besley is closely tied to state capacity, accountability and the political-agency framework. The credit is plausibly shared among the three, though others (e.g. Alesina, deceased) contributed.
assessment.maturity: The research dates from the 1990s onward and is well established, with extensive empirical testing and follow-up. The 2024 prize on institutions and prosperity partly overlaps thematically, which could cut either way.
uncertainties: Thematic proximity to the 2024 award may reduce appetite for another institutions-related prize.
Identification in the cross-country constitutional comparisons is debated.
Persson's institutional proximity to the committee, and my own political-science background, are disclosed and not adjudicated here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data were used to measure intergenerational mobility, its geographic variation and the causal effect of neighbourhoods. This opened a new empirical research agenda and drew strong policy attention. It is methodologically innovative and widely replicated in other countries.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the clear intellectual lead. Hendren and Friedman are major collaborators on the neighbourhood-effects and mobility papers. Katz also appears in the credited list but is placed in B019.
assessment.maturity: Most of the work is from after about 2014, so the confirmation period is shorter than for older candidates. Replications and extensions are accumulating.
uncertainties: The work may be seen as too recent relative to other candidates.
Credit is spread across a large collaborative team.
Some mobility measures and neighbourhood-effect estimates have drawn methodological critiques.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic panel GMM estimators (Arellano-Bond, Arellano-Bover, Blundell-Bond) became standard tools across applied economics, particularly in growth, finance and industrial organisation. The influence is very broad, although the contribution is econometric and instrumental.
assessment.attribution: The estimator papers point clearly to Arellano, Bond and Blundell. Blundell has additional distinct contributions elsewhere, as in B037.
assessment.maturity: The methods date from the 1990s and have extensive use, plus well-known limitations such as instrument proliferation and weak instruments.
uncertainties: The committee may prefer a methodological prize with more conceptual depth.
Misuse in applied work does not diminish the contribution but may affect perceived impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The alternating-offers bargaining model gave a tractable non-cooperative foundation for bargaining and is embedded in labour, trade, political and market-design models. The Rubinstein-Wolinsky decentralised market analysis connected bargaining and search. This is high-impact, foundational theory.
assessment.attribution: Rubinstein's 1982 model is the key contribution, and Ståhl's related earlier work is acknowledged in the literature. Wolinsky has a well-defined joint contribution on markets. Binmore's role was mainly interpretation and extension, so he is a weaker fit.
assessment.maturity: More than forty years of use make the contribution fully mature.
uncertainties: Game theory has had several recent prizes, which may affect committee balance.
Rubinstein's later work is largely on bounded rationality, so the case rests on the earlier work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The BLP demand-estimation approach and the dynamic-oligopoly estimation framework made structural analysis of differentiated-product markets practical. They are central to merger analysis, antitrust and empirical industrial organisation. The influence on policy practice is substantial.
assessment.attribution: Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes form the core BLP trio. Pakes also has separate work on dynamic games and on estimation. Bresnahan, Benkard, Reiss and Levin are strong contributors but fall outside the three-name cap.
assessment.maturity: The methods date from the 1990s and are very widely adopted, so maturity is high.
uncertainties: The credited list is wide, so the attribution cut is contestable.
The structural-versus-reduced-form debate could affect reception.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The collateral-constraint credit-cycle model shows how small shocks are amplified through asset prices and borrowing limits. It became a cornerstone of macro-finance and was clearly validated in thinking about the 2008 crisis.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore's 1997 paper is the origin of the mechanism. The Bernanke-Gertler-Gilchrist financial accelerator is a related but distinct strand, and Bernanke has already been recognised.
assessment.maturity: The model is nearly three decades old and had major empirical and policy relevance after 2008, so maturity is good.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier 2022 prize on banks and financial crises could weigh against it.
It is unclear whether the committee would treat the Kiyotaki-Moore and financial-accelerator strands as one body of work.
